Regional results
The United States, China and Europe are projected to remain the largest regions for data
centre electricity demand over the coming years. However, other regions are experiencing
strong growth in data centre development, positioning them to play increasingly important
roles in the global data centre landscape. A notable example is Southeast Asia, where
electricity demand from data centres is expected to more than double by 2030, partially due
to the presence of a regional hub in Singapore and southern Malaysia (Johor province).
China and the United States are the most significant regions for data centre electricity
consumption growth, accounting for nearly 80% of global growth to 2030. Consumption
increases by around 240 TWh (up 130%) in the United States, compared to the 2024 level
Figure 2.12
). In China it increases by around 175 TWh (up 170%). In Europe it grows by more
than 45 TWh (up 70%). Japan increases by around 15 TWh (up 80%).
Comparing data centre electricity consumption normalised per capita can give a sense of the
importance of this sector in different economies. Africa has the lowest consumption at less
than 1 kWh of data centre electricity consumption per capita in 2024, rising to slightly less
than 2 kWh per capita by the end of the decade. However, there are strong differences within
